# `nlink-lab bundle`

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
Keep a lab's failure bundle: everything needed to debug it.

`DIR/<lab>/` gets `summary.txt` (the seed and how to replay it), `topology.nll`, `status.json`, `events.ndjson`, and per node its addresses, routes, rules, nftables ruleset, qdiscs, conntrack table and process logs, as JSON from the host's `ip`, `nft` and `tc` run in the node's namespace. A failing `nlink-lab test` and `#[lab_test]` keep one by themselves.

Usage: nlink-lab bundle [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -L, --lab <LAB>
          The lab. Default: `$NLINK_LAB`, then the one `nlink-lab use` selected, then the only running lab

  -o, --output <DIR>
          Where to write it: `DIR/<lab>/`. Default `$NLINK_LAB_BUNDLE_DIR`, else `./nlink-lab-bundles`

      --archive
          Also pack it as `<lab>.tar.gz` beside the directory

      --reason <TEXT>
          Why, for the summary (default: "on demand")

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
